text:
MPC bounced back 4.6% today after hitting a five-day low on November 6th, when the stock lost nearly 18% from its peak. The recovery came as oil prices stabilized—U.S. crude held steady around $99.64 a barrel—and refinery utilization remained solid at 94.5%, suggesting steady demand for refined products. The timing of this rebound coincides with news that U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks remain stalled, which historically supports oil prices by reducing near-term supply concerns.

The stock's broader two-week decline reflects the market's reaction to the earnings report and quarterly results released November 3rd, combined with uncertainty around the political transition and what energy policy might look like under a new administration. Refiners like Marathon are sensitive to shifts in regulation and fuel demand expectations, so the shift in congressional control and early signals about energy priorities likely weighed on the stock through the week—though today's rebound suggests some stabilization as oil prices found a floor.
